context: Block-Skill adjacency matrix showing which of 105 D3.js visualization blocks use each of 26 skills, with cells colored by skill category (6 categories) and interactive sorting/zoom/tooltip.
first_impression: Binary presence/absence encoding is intrinsically honest — no quantitative distortion is possible — and the implementation backs this up with data-driven scaleBand domains and a key function on cell joins.
what_works: Color encodes categorical skill group correctly with no quantitative misuse; scaleBand domains are fully data-driven from sorted arrays, skill usage counts are computed from actual data, and the cell key function `d => block.id|skill` is present for object constancy.
what_doesnt: The `g.selectAll('*').remove()` full-clear on every sort render makes the cell key function a no-op (no transitions, object constancy is never exercised); the categoryColors object contains a duplicate key for 'Making it legible' (lines 175-176), a copy-paste error that is harmless only because the category name appears once in the data.
